newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Huntington not seeking big purchases.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Huntington not seeking big purchases.

text.p: Huntington Bancshares Inc said Monday it will not be seeking further major acquisitions for the time being, after announcing a deal to buy First Michigan Bank Corp for about $900 million.
"At this time, we are not looking at anything on this scale," Zuher Sofia, president of Columbus, Ohio-based Huntington, said in an interview.
But the $21 billion asset bank holding company would still consider "fill-in" acquisitions in its three target markets of Ohio, Michigan and Florida, he said.

Sofia said Huntington expects the acquisition of Holland, Michigan-based First Michigan will add one percent to 1998 earnings and four percent in 1999, with the accretion figures based on conservative estimates.
"When you take a look at this particular transaction, we were able to make it -- in a very conservative way -- accretive," Sofia said.
Among cost savings will be the consolidation of First Michigan's 14 bank charters into one Huntington bank, he said.
He also questioned analysts that said the deal, which values First Michigan at about 19 times 1996 earnings, was expensive.
"Pricey is in the eye of the beholder," Sofia said. "Huntington is not paying much premium over the market."
The deal was valued at $31.50 a share based on Huntington's closing price Friday. First Michigan traded as high as $30.75 in recent weeks on takeover speculation, analysts said.
"Taking this pricing, are you able to create value and are you able to sustain it? We think we are," Sofia said.
Huntington shares were down 3/8 at 29-5/8 Monday, while First Michigan shares fell one to 29-3/4.
